title: Shanghai Jiao Tong's AutoDNA: AI agents run a DNA lab across 20+ instruments
summary: A Nature paper presents AutoDNA, a lab where a team of LLM agents plans and runs nucleic-acid synthesis, amplification, transcription and sequencing from a typed prompt. A virtual copy of the lab checks each procedure before robots execute it.

claims.text: Published in Nature on 4 Nov 2026 (doi 10.1038/s41586-026-11228-6)
Coordinates more than 20 types of instruments; 36Kr reports over 11,000 experiment steps (step counts differ between outlets)
A preprint version was posted on arXiv in July 2025 (2507.02379)
Humans still restocked reagents and removed waste (Singularity Hub's account)
Nature's news story calls it an AI-native self-driving biology lab built around AI from the start

why_it_matters: A peer-reviewed multi-agent lab that schedules many instruments end to end; the pattern (agents + digital-twin check) is what ADME workcells would need, not yet shown there.

title: Nature: AI agents plan a robot lab in a digital twin, then run it

summary: PyLabRobot merged 34 commits from 8 to 13 Nov, adding drivers for the Formulatrix Mantis dispenser and Inheco ODTC thermocycler and a TCP transport for Hamilton machines. 23 of the 34 commits credit an AI coding assistant as co-author.

claims.text: Mantis: connect, identify, plate clamp, RFID chip tags, arm and Z bring-up, sequencer (PRs 1612, 1621-1623)

title: PyLabRobot now requires drivers to restore a device's original state
summary: PyLabRobot's device-driver guide adds a rule: a driver must leave an instrument as it found it, restoring any changed memory, registers or settings at the end of setup/stop or of each command, including after errors.

claims.text: Rule added to docs/contributor_guide/device-driver-guide.md on 11 Nov 2026 (PR 1616)
Drivers must read and save original values and restore those exact values, not assumed defaults
Cleanup must also run on errors, cancellation and partial setup failures

why_it_matters: Shared instruments in DMPK labs also run vendor software; a driver that silently changes settings could corrupt the next validated method.

title: Explainer: how PyLabRobot finds and talks to Hamilton machines over a network
summary: New PyLabRobot code finds Hamilton instruments with a UDP broadcast and talks to them in plain-text lines over TCP. Because replies return in completion order, every command carries an id and a background reader matches each reply to its command.

claims.text: Discovery broadcasts on UDP port 34569; machines answer with bdc_ key/value pairs (IP, system id, module name, MAC)
Text protocol over TCP defaults to port 24652, one CRLF-terminated ASCII line per command or reply, no handshake or keepalive
Router docstring: several commands can be in flight; STAR and Vantage are reached over USB, a 'STAR V' over a socket
Users can connect by machine name instead of IP via resolve_host

why_it_matters: Network discovery plus async replies is what lets a scheduler drive several liquid handlers at once; the 'STAR V' mention is unexplained in public sources.
